messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Yes this is a true bug. Sorry for that.

It was already fixed in my dev version but it is now very difficult to submit a new version to CRAN.

The solution is to move

  if(is.null(at)) {x <- ((0:(n-1))*f/n/1000)[1:(n%/%2)]} # if at null then complete signal
    else {x <- ((0:(wl-1))*f/wl/1000)[1:(wl%/%2)]} # if at not null then use of a wl

above

  # DB
  if(!is.null(dB))
...

HTH

Jerome

De: "Roelant Ossewaarde" <roel...@gmail.com>
À: "seewave GROUP" <see...@googlegroups.com>
Envoyé: Jeudi 8 Novembre 2018 12:32:13
Objet: [seewave] Use of dBweight in spec() function

Hi,
I am trying to convert the output of spec() into dB-values.

spec() has code to do this starting at lines 5997 of seewave.R:

  # DB
  if(!is.null(dB))
    {
      y <- ifelse(y==0, yes=1e-6, no=y)  # replaces 0 values in spectra that cannot be processed by log10()
      if(is.null(dBref)) {y <- 20*log10(y)} else {y <- 20*log10(y/dBref)}
      if(dB!="max0")
          {
            if(dB == "A") y <- dBweight(x*1000, dBref = y)$A
            if(dB == "B") y <- dBweight(x*1000, dBref = y)$B
            if(dB == "C") y <- dBweight(x*1000, dBref = y)$C
            if(dB == "D") y <- dBweight(x*1000, dBref = y)$D
          }
    }

This code results in an error, because it refers to variable x which has not been defined up until this point.

I considered simply correcting it in:

if(dB == "A") y <- dBweight(y*1000, dBref = dBref)$A

But the documentation says that the first argument to dBweight wants a frequency (which could be y at this point, since it is the result of a FFT a few lines before) but the y-argument is transformed to a dB-value in the line that starts with  if(is.null(dBref)).

Is this a known issue?

Kind regards,

Roelant.

messages.subject: moving axis labels on the oscillogram
messages.subject_clean: moving axis labels on the oscillogram
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have been making small plots that have a spectrogram above an oscilliogram. I would like to move the axis labels closer to their axes, but changing the parameter mgp only moves the y-axis label in the spectrogram.  I have tried various other things with par(), with no success. I do not just want to make the margins wider. Help much appreciated.

data(tico)
f <-t...@samp.rate
par(mgp=c(2.0, 0.5, 0))
spectro(tico, f=f, wl=512, ovlp=85, collevels=seq(-30,0,1), cexlab = 2, cexaxis = 1.8, osc=TRUE, colgrid="grey75", colwave="black", colaxis="black", collab="black", colbg="white", tlab = "Time (Sec)", flab = "Frequency (kHz)", alab = "Amplitude", flim=c(0,10), scale=FALSE, heights = c(2, 1))

Thanks, K

messages.subject_clean: [seewave] moving axis labels on the oscillogram
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kyle,
Yes, this is because the labels of the oscillogram of spectro() are not added with a conventional xlab or ylab argument but calling mtext().
Here is a solution, not very nice I have to admit.
Best
Jerome

---

par(mgp=c(2.0, 0.5, 0))
spectro(tico, f=f, wl=512, ovlp=85, collevels=seq(-30,0,1),
        cexlab = 2, cexaxis = 1.8, osc=TRUE,
        colgrid="grey75", colwave="black", colaxis="black", collab="black", colbg="white",

        tlab = "", flab = "Frequency (kHz)", alab = "",

        flim=c(0,10), scale=FALSE, heights = c(2, 1))

mtext(text="Time (Sec)", side=1, line=9, cex=2)
mtext(text="Ampitude", side=2, at=-1.5, line=2, cex=2, las=0)
